thread:
marta: quick q — onboarding the new open-weights model. where are the canonical weight files supposed to live? HF repo or our s3 mirror? I found one copy in hf://open-models/galah-9b but the CI mirror path is s3://redwood-artifacts/models/galah-9b/v1/weights.pt
devon: canonical source should be HF for provenance, but we mirror to s3 for serving. plan: pull from HF, verify checksum, then push to s3://redwood-artifacts/ and pin manifest.
marta: got it. I pulled s3 copy and when running onboarding sanity the sha256 differs from HF release notes. any ideas?
ryan: did you check for sharded vs single-file weights? HF release has 8 shard files (p1, p2...) but the s3 copy looks like a single consolidated weights.pt — different binaries => checksum mismatch expected.
marta: ah ok. the onboarding CI expects shards. we should update CI or mirror the shards exactly. which do we prefer?
devon: prefer mirroring exact HF artifacts (shards + tokenizer + config). Consolidation should be a separate build step and signed. keeps provenance clear.
sam: +1. also noticed tokenizer wordpiece offsets disagree with our tokenization tests when using the s3 consolidated file. tokenizer.json on HF is v2 but s3 has an older v1. That explains some eval diffs.
marta: ugh tokenizer mismatch is nasty. do we have an automated check for tokenizer version in the onboarding pipeline?
olivia: not currently. suggest adding a simple check: compare tokenizer.json['model_max_length'] and tokenizer['version'] and run a tiny tokenization roundtrip on a few fixture prompts. fail the onboarding if mismatch.
sam: example snippet for CI (bash):
```bash
# verify tokenizer matches HF
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/models/galah-9b/v1/tokenizer.json ./tokenizer.json
python -c "import json; j=json.load(open('tokenizer.json')); assert j.get('version','').startswith('2'), 'tokenizer version mismatch'"
```
ryan: also update model-metadata.yaml to include: weights: [list of shard keys], tokenizer_key, config_key, and sha256s for each file. CI can then fetch and compare each sha256.
marta: who can push the correct shard files to s3 and add the checksums? @devon?
devon: I can. need an iam role for the mirror job though — currently the sync user only has read on hf-sync bucket. @olivia can we get write perms for ci-mirror-role on s3://redwood-artifacts/models/galah-9b/* ?
olivia: filing a quick perms request. ETA ~2 hours. putting patch in the infra queue.
artifact-bot: manifest generated: {"hf_src":"hf://open-models/galah-9b","s3_prefix":"s3://redwood-artifacts/models/galah-9b/v1/","files":["pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin","pytorch_model-00002-of-00008.bin","tokenizer.json","config.json"],"checksums":["sha256:abc123...","sha256:def456...","sha256:tok789...","sha256:cfg012..."]} :robot_face:
marta: perfect. once perms landed, devon can run mirror and then I'll kick the onboarding CI.
devon: posting the presign command I'll use for temporary public fetching during the sync (internal only):
```bash
aws s3 presign s3://redwood-artifacts/models/galah-9b/v1/pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin --expires-in 3600
```
sam: for HF pulls, use huggingface-cli to download LFS files reliably:
```bash
hf_repo="open-models/galah-9b"
huggingface-cli repo clone $hf_repo tmp && rsync -av tmp/ ./model_files/ && rm -rf tmp
```
ryan: adding a note — when mirroring, preserve HF filenames exactly. our serving runtime expects shard naming pattern for kv cache mapping. renaming will break warmstart.
marta: noted. last QA: config.json on s3 had "torch_dtype":"float16" but HF says "float32". which should we trust?
devon: trust HF. I'll reupload matching config.json and include a diff in the manifest.
olivia: perms approved and applied to ci-mirror-role. devon you should have write now.
devon: starting mirror job now. I'll post logs here when done.
artifact-bot: mirror job completed for galah-9b v1 — uploaded 11 files, verified 11 checksums, manifest updated.
marta: thanks! I'll run the onboarding tests and report back if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
sam: quick follow-up task for devex: add tokenizer version check and a small tokenization roundtrip to onboarding smoke tests. tagging @devex in a follow-up PR.
marta: that's all from me, closing the loop once CI passes.
